item.title: Global Market: China and Hong Kong shares weaken as stable growth eases stimulus bets
item.description: China and Hong Kong stocks weakened on Tuesday, joining a broader retreat in the region, after Beijing kept key lending rates unchanged and stronger GDP data dampened
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: HONG KONG, - China and Hong Kong stocks weakened on Tuesday, joining a broader retreat in the region, after Beijing kept key lending rates unchanged and stronger GDP data dampened expectations for additional stimulus* China's blue-chip CSI300 Index dropped 0.5% by the lunch break, while the Shanghai Composite Index was 0.1% weaker** Dragging the broader market lower, the CSI Banks Index and the financial sector were both down 1.4%. The gold-related sector weakened 1.2% as bullion prices continued to slip** The startup board ChiNext Composite index was higher by 0.3% to recover from a 14-month low, and Shanghai's tech-focused STAR50 index was up 0.8% ** In Hong Kong, the city's benchmark Hang Seng was down 1%, and the Hang Seng Tech Index slid 1.2% to a two-year low** In a sign that policymakers are in no rush to roll out further monetary easing following the strong GDP reading, China left its benchmark lending rates unchanged for the 17th straight month in October on Tuesday, in line with market expectations** That came after China's economy rebounded from a three-year low last quarter, expanding 4.5% and beating estimates, as robust exports offset tepid domestic demand** The stable headline growth lessens the urgency to unleash a new volley of fiscal and monetary stimulus , analysts at Maybank said in a note** Without additional stimulus, sluggish domestic investment and consumption will still lead to slightly slower growth, they added** The smaller Beijing Stock Exchange 50 Index jumped more than 4% after China's securities regulator, the CSRC, said it would launch an ETF tracking the index to support the bourse's development** Asian stocks retreated broadly on Tuesday while oil rose as geopolitical risks rattled sentiment ahead of key results from AI bellwether companies

item.title: Korea’s KOSPI crashes another 5% as AI rout deepens; AI bellwether down over 40% from peak
item.description: Chip heavyweight SK Hynix Inc. headed for its lowest close since April. Data-center infrastructure company Elice Inc. plunged as much as 32% in its trading debut in Seoul. Both AI bellwethers SK Hynix and Samsung have plunged 35% and 22%, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Veer Sharma
item.content:encoded: South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI fell 5% on Tuesday as a chip-led sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks deepened, cutting its 2026 gains to about 30% from roughly 116% at its record close in June. The index has dipped over 40% from its peak of 9,386 earlier this year. Chip heavyweight SK Hynix Inc. headed for its lowest close since April. Data-center infrastructure company Elice Inc. plunged as much as 32% in its trading debut in Seoul. Both AI bellwethers SK Hynix and Samsung have plunged 35% and 22%, respectively. The index now trades about 39% below that peak. The decline gathered pace in July, when the KOSPI fell 22%, and extended into October, with the index losing another 17% through October 16.Read more: Global Market: Japan's Nikkei falls as higher yields, inflation fears weighWhat’s driving the sell-off?The latest leg of the decline follows a global sell-off in AI-linked stocks, which last week wiped out more than $1 trillion in market value from 20 of the world’s most valuable AI and semiconductor companies. South Korea has been particularly vulnerable to the rout because of its heavy exposure to memory chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. The two companies accounted for 44% of the KOSPI in May. The sell-off gathered momentum as investors grew increasingly concerned about the credit risks associated with heavy AI spending. Further, stronger-than-expected US inflation data has added to the pressure, sending the index down 7.57% to 5,554.22.OpenAI’s revenue projections add to investor concernsQuestions over the sustainability of AI spending intensified after OpenAI told investors last week that its annualised revenue for September was nearly $50 billion, below the figure it had indicated earlier, Reuters reported.At a separate event, the company had previously told investors that its September revenue run rate was approaching $70 billion. The discrepancy largely stemmed from an effort to make a direct comparison with revenue figures from rival Anthropic, according to the Reuters report.The figures have added to investor scrutiny of the financial assumptions underpinning the AI rally, particularly as companies continue to commit substantial sums to infrastructure and computing capacity.AI’s next hurdle may be the cost of capitalConcerns about financing are also coming from within the semiconductor industry. Earlier this week, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said capital could become a bigger constraint on AI expansion than shortages of semiconductors, memory chips or electricity.Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan echoed the concern, pointing to rising capital costs and the need for companies making heavy AI investments to demonstrate adequate returns.The warnings come as investors reassess whether the pace of AI investment can be sustained amid stretched valuations, intensifying competition and uncertainty over when the spending will translate into profits.What lies ahead for AI stocks?The debate over AI valuations is also prompting calls for investors to diversify beyond the sector. In his latest GREED & fear note, Jefferies’ Global Head of Equity Strategy Chris Wood highlighted a warning from the firm’s global quantitative strategy team that “it has become time to diversify beyond AI.”The report projects earnings growth for global AI stocks to slow from nearly 100% in 2026 to 30% in 2027 and 22% in 2028. By comparison, earnings growth for global stocks excluding AI is expected to decline from 16% this year to 9% in both 2027 and 2028.Valuations further underline the divide. Global AI stocks trade at about 23 times forward earnings on an equal-weighted basis, compared with 13 times for the global ex-AI basket, according to the report.Wood has pointed to rising borrowing costs as a central factor in the AI spending boom, raising questions about how long the market will continue to finance the trade.With earnings growth expected to moderate and AI stocks trading at a substantial premium to the broader market, the sustainability of the rally increasingly hinges on companies delivering returns on their investments, alongside the availability and cost of financing.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. item.title: Brokerages back ICICI Bank on strong Q2 earnings, see HDFC Bank recovery ahead
item.description: Brokerages remain optimistic about ICICI Bank's strong earnings and asset quality after the recent quarter. However, HDFC Bank's profit growth was modest, and margins are under pressure, leading to a more cautious outlook. Despite this, both banks have attractive valuations and positive earnings recovery prospects. On Monday, both stocks experienced declines, along with broader market indices. Analysts highlight potential upsides for both banks based on target prices.
item.dc:creator: ET Bureau
item.content:encoded: Top brokerages remained bullish on ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank after their September quarter earnings, though their assessments of the two lenders differed sharply. Analysts were upbeat about ICICI Bank’s stronger-than-expected earnings and resilient asset quality, reinforcing its position as a preferred stock among large private sector banks. Their assessment of HDFC Bank was more measured after the lender reported modest profit growth and pressure on margins. However, attractive valuations, prospects of an earnings recovery and expectations of improved execution amid leadership changes helped sustain the positive outlook.Read more: Banking stocks, high oil prices drag Indian markets lowerBoth stocks closed lower on Monday, with ICICI Bank falling 1.1% to Rs 1382 and HDFC Bank declining 2.3% to 712. The benchmark Nifty fell 1.11%, while the Bank Nifty slipped 0.6%. According to Bloomberg data, target prices for ICICI Bank imply a potential upside of 24-48%. For HDFC Bank, the target prices indicate potential gains of 17-78%.135059105
